description: SPDX licence allowlist for npm dependencies (gate L1, R-SEC-7). A package passes when its licence expression evaluates to true: OR needs one allowed alternative, AND needs every term allowed. Unknown, UNLICENSED, missing or non-SPDX licence metadata fails.

rationale.permissive: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, 0BSD, Zlib, BlueOak-1.0.0 and Unicode-3.0 are permissive licences with attribution-only or no conditions.
rationale.mpl_2_0: MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: it is allowed for unmodified use of the package (e.g. axe-core in the frontend test tooling). Modifying an MPL-2.0 file and distributing it triggers source-disclosure for that file; such a change needs compliance review.
rationale.data_licences: CC0-1.0 and CC-BY-4.0 cover data packages (language-subtag-registry, caniuse-lite); CC-BY-4.0 requires attribution, which the third-party notice generation must carry.
rationale.python_2_0: Python-2.0 covers argparse (a port of the Python module); it is permissive.
rationale.excluded: Strong and network copyleft (GPL-*, AGPL-*), LGPL-* , SSPL, BUSL, CC-BY-NC-*, proprietary and UNLICENSED are not allowed. LGPL is excluded on purpose: whether dynamic or optional use satisfies it is a legal decision, so an LGPL dependency must go through a dated waiver in docs/waivers.yml (owner, issue, expiry <= 90 days) instead of a standing allowance.
rationale.scope: The list mirrors the cargo-deny allowlist in deny.toml by intent, not by file: Rust crates are judged by cargo-deny with deny.toml, npm packages by this file. Both are reviewed together.
rationale.note: This is an engineering control derived from the licences observed in frontend/package-lock.json and tools/legal-audit/package-lock.json on 2026-10-23. It is not legal advice; the allowlist needs sign-off by the compliance owner (Progress.md D-5).
